sections.h2: Who handles a Mesquite tax bill
sections.html:
Mesquite straddles two counties, Dallas and Kaufman, so check which one holds your parcel before you call anyone. The county decides who values the house and who takes the check, and the city's tax page prints a separate rate table for each side.

The state itself collects no property tax. A county appraisal district sets a value on the house each January 1, and then five local bodies, from the city to Parkland Hospital, apply their own rates to it.

  • Dallas County parcels: Dallas Central Appraisal District, 214-631-0520, for value and exemptions; the Dallas County tax office, 214-653-7811, for city and Mesquite ISD bills.
  • Kaufman County parcels: Kaufman Central Appraisal District in the town of Kaufman, 972-932-6081.
  • Past-due accounts: Grimes & Linebarger, LLP at 120 West Main, Suite 201 in Mesquite, 469-942-2011.

The city's tax office cannot process exemption forms for you. Those go to the appraisal district.

The city's 2025 rate is $0.7046920 per $100 of assessed value. The rest of the bill depends on the county line, because Mesquite ISD, Dallas College and Parkland Hospital charge the same on either side of it.

Recent state-level changes have noticeably lowered resident bills. The larger homestead exemption and the extra help for owners over 65 or disabled both cut school taxes. The city's tax page links to estimating tools for each county, so you can test your own parcel instead of guessing at a total.

Other taxing units may be added to these totals on some parcels, so look up your own parcel at the appraisal district before you quote a figure to a buyer.

Statements are mailed in October and can be paid on arrival. Dallas County treats an account as late once January 31 has gone by, and it reads the postmark on a mailed check. Not receiving the statement does not excuse the tax or the late charges.

February 1 brings a penalty of 6 percent plus interest of 1 percent. Interest keeps adding a point a month with no stopping point, and the penalty rises a point a month until it tops out at 12 percent in July.

  • Dallas County hands non-business accounts to its collection attorney on July 1, and the attorney's fee can reach 20 percent.
  • To ask for a waiver of the charges, send the request in writing before day 181 of delinquency and settle the tax within 21 days of finding out it was late.
  • Some collectors write installment agreements running as long as 36 months, and a residence homestead is the only case where one must be offered.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may split the bill into four payments.

Start with age. The city lists a $65,000 exemption for homeowners over 65 and a $15,000 exemption for disabled persons, and a person gets one or the other. Either one also brings a ceiling: city and school taxes stay at what you paid in the first qualifying year until you build onto the house or move.

School taxes have a state-set break of their own, $140,000 off a residence homestead and $60,000 more for older or disabled owners.

  • Disabled veteran exemptions are $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating, rising to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a 100 percent rating can wipe out the homestead's taxable value.
  • A homestead's appraised value is capped at a 10 percent yearly rise, beginning the year after the first exemption.
  • Heirs whose names are not on the recorded deed send the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: When to file a value protest
sections.html:
File the written protest with the Appraisal Review Board by May 15, or 30 days after delivery of the notice when that is later. Homestead notices start going out around April 1, and notices for other property follow near May 1.

Dallas County's tax office refers all protest questions to the appraisal districts. A Dallas County parcel is disputed at Dallas Central Appraisal District and a Kaufman County parcel at Kaufman Central Appraisal District. If you lose at the board, you can go to district court, ask for binding arbitration, or use the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values above $1,000,000. Pay the portion nobody disputes before the cutoff, or the appeal will not protect you from penalties.

Mesquite had 150,693 residents in the July 2025 estimate, barely changed from 150,108 at the 2020 census. Owners occupy 62.8 percent of homes, and the middle owned-home value is $245,700. Middle gross rent is $1,513 and middle household income is $72,537. About 11.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, the group eligible for the city's larger exemption.

sections.h2: What a Mesquite seller should check before closing
sections.html:
The tax lien keys off who owns the house on January 1. Whoever holds title that day owes the whole year, even when the sale closes in March. Ask the title company how the bill will be divided with the buyer, and read the payoff lines of its commitment.

A buyer closing after the new year may apply for the homestead exemption immediately if the seller never had it. Sellers should confirm what is owed with the Dallas County Tax Office, or the Kaufman County tax office for a Kaufman parcel.

When the account has already gone to the collection attorney, ask for a written payoff itemizing penalty, interest and court costs. The title company needs that figure to clear the lien when the sale funds.

Before you list, gather the latest statement from each taxing unit, your homestead exemption confirmation if you have one, and any protest paperwork from the spring. Tell the title company if a protest is still open, since a successful one changes the tax figure that the closing statement is built around, and note the hearing date for the buyer.

faqs.q: Why does the Kaufman County side of Mesquite show a higher total rate?
faqs.a: Only the county line changes. The city's table shows 0.2155000 for Dallas County and 0.4275260 for Kaufman County, which produces totals of 2.3456670 and 2.5576930.

faqs.q: Until what date can Mesquite taxes be paid without charges?
faqs.a: January 31. Charges begin February 1 and grow each month into July.

faqs.q: How much does Mesquite exempt for homeowners over 65?
faqs.a: The city exempts $65,000 for owners over 65 and $15,000 for disabled persons, and one person gets only one of the two. Mesquite ISD applies its own state-mandated amounts.

faqs.q: Where do I pick up a homestead exemption form for a house in Mesquite?
faqs.a: Call the appraisal district for your county, Dallas Central at 214-631-0520 or Kaufman Central at 972-932-6081. The city's tax office does not issue them.

faqs.q: Can a Mesquite house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company gets a payoff from the collection attorney and pays it at closing, since the lien follows the property until then.
